display_name: Code Review Agent — Single-Pass vs Multi-Pass

workflow.name: codereview-agent-comparison
workflow.description: Compare two code review agent strategies: a single-pass holistic review vs a multi-pass strategy that runs specialized sub-agents for linting, security scanning, logic analysis, and final summarization. Demonstrates deep nesting, sub_agent event types, and the quality-vs-cost tradeoff where the more expensive approach catches more issues.

eval_run.name: Single-Pass vs Multi-Pass — Code Review Quality
eval_run.description: The single-pass strategy reads the diff once and produces a review. The multi-pass strategy delegates to specialized sub-agents (linter, security scanner, logic reviewer) then synthesizes. Multi-pass costs more but catches security and edge-case issues the single-pass misses.

cases.label: auth-middleware-pr
cases.input: Review PR #347: Add JWT authentication middleware to the Express API. Changes: new auth.js middleware, route protection for /api/users and /api/admin, token refresh endpoint.

output_data.text: PR adds JWT auth middleware to Express. I'll review the diff holistically for correctness, style, and common auth pitfalls.

Reviewing all changes together. Found: generally clean implementation, good use of express middleware pattern. Suggestions: add rate limiting to token refresh, consider using httpOnly cookies instead of localStorage for token storage, add input validation on login endpoint.
Composing review with 3 suggestions. Approve with minor comments. No blocking issues identified.

JWT auth PR requires careful multi-pass review. Plan:
1. Lint pass: style, naming, structure
2. Security pass: auth-specific vulnerabilities
3. Logic pass: correctness, edge cases
4. Synthesize findings into final review

input_data.task: Review code style, naming conventions, and structure of the JWT auth PR

findings: Inconsistent error message format in auth.js
Missing JSDoc on exported middleware function

details: consistent-return: missing return in error branch

output_data.text: Two style issues found: inconsistent error messages (some use objects, others strings) and missing JSDoc on the exported verifyToken function.

input_data.task: Security audit of JWT auth middleware — check for common auth vulnerabilities

findings: JWT secret in config.js not from env var
Missing CSRF protection on refresh endpoint
Token stored in localStorage — XSS vulnerability

output_data.text: Four security issues found, one critical. The hardcoded JWT secret is a deployment blocker. Token expiry and CSRF protections are high-priority fixes. localStorage vs httpOnly cookie is a design discussion.

input_data.task: Review business logic correctness and edge cases in JWT auth flow

findings: Race condition on concurrent token refresh
No handling of clock skew in token validation
Admin route protection checks role but not token validity first

output_data.text: Tracing the authentication flow: login → token issued → middleware validates → refresh flow. Checking each transition for correctness.

Three logic issues: 1) Concurrent refresh requests could issue multiple new tokens (race condition), 2) No clock skew tolerance — tokens may fail validation across server instances, 3) Admin middleware checks req.user.role before checking if token is valid at all.

Combining findings from all three passes. Total: 9 issues (1 critical, 2 high, 3 medium, 3 low). The single-pass approach would have caught ~3 of these. Recommending: request changes, with the JWT secret and token expiry as blocking issues.

cases.label: database-migration-pr
cases.input: Review PR #412: Add user_preferences table and migration script. Adds a new table with JSON column for preferences, migration to create it, and API endpoints to read/write preferences.

output_data.text: DB migration PR adding a user preferences table with JSON storage. Reviewing for migration safety, schema design, and API correctness.

Review of migration and endpoints. Clean implementation. Suggestions: add an index on user_id for the preferences table, consider adding a size limit on the JSON column to prevent abuse, add NOT NULL constraint on user_id.
Composing review with 3 suggestions. Approve with suggestions. Migration is safe, endpoints are correct.

Database migration PR needs careful review. Plan:
1. Lint: SQL style, Python code quality
2. Security: SQL injection, input validation, authorization
3. Logic: migration safety, rollback strategy, data integrity
4. Synthesize

input_data.task: Review SQL migration style and Python code quality

findings: Migration SQL uses implicit column order in INSERT — should be explicit

output_data.text: Migration SQL is acceptable but uses implicit column ordering. One Python docstring missing.

input_data.task: Security audit of preferences API — check for injection, auth, data exposure

findings: No authorization check — any user can read/write other users' preferences
JSON input not validated — potential for oversized payloads
No rate limiting on write endpoint

details: CRITICAL: Missing ownership check on user_id parameter
HIGH: No payload size limit on JSON body

output_data.text: Critical: The PUT /preferences/:userId endpoint doesn't verify that the authenticated user matches the userId parameter. Any authenticated user can overwrite anyone else's preferences. This is an IDOR vulnerability.

input_data.task: Review migration safety, rollback strategy, and data integrity for user_preferences table

findings: No default value for preferences column — NULL on insert

output_data.text: Migration creates table but has no down/rollback script. In production, every migration should be reversible. Also missing the index on user_id which will be needed for the FK lookup.
No default value for the JSON preferences column. If application code doesn't always supply a value, rows with NULL preferences will cause runtime errors in the API endpoint.

Multi-pass found 7 issues total (1 critical IDOR, 2 high, 2 medium, 2 low). The IDOR vulnerability is a blocking issue — single-pass would likely miss it since it requires tracing the auth flow across files. Recommending: request changes.
